name: Butylated hydroxytoluene
aliases: E321, BHT, butylated hydroxytoluene, hidroxitolueno butilado, 2,6-di-tert-butyl-p-cresol
what_is: BHT (E321) is a synthetic antioxidant added to foods containing fats and oils to slow oxidation and stop them from going rancid.
why_botia: BHT prevents fats from going rancid, like BHA, but it is a different compound and behaves differently. At high doses in animals it affected the liver and thyroid, and in some laboratory tests it can weakly mimic or block estrogen signals — a finding worth watching, not proof that eating BHT disrupts hormones in people. IARC classifies BHT in Group 3 because the evidence was not enough to classify its carcinogenicity; that does not mean it was shown to be harmless. JECFA set an acceptable daily intake of 0–0.3 mg/kg body weight per day.
can_1: Detect E321, BHT and its declared chemical names in the ingredient list.
can_2: Show the animal and laboratory findings, IARC's Group 3 classification and JECFA's acceptable daily intake of 0–0.3 mg/kg body weight per day.
cannot_1: Determine how much BHT is present in a particular product when the amount is not declared.
cannot_2: Treat laboratory hormonal activity or animal findings as proof that BHT causes the same effects in a person eating a particular food.
